subject: Urgent: Emergency heap-guard activation — short notice maintenance and actions
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Zoe Patel <zoe.patel@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 02:15:00 -0800
Subject: Urgent: Emergency heap-guard activation — short notice maintenance and actions

Hi Zoe —

Quick heads-up: our runtime telemetry picked up a progressive heap-growth pattern on the inference pool serving your production workspace (region us-west) that can lead to degraded tail latency and rare OOM-triggered restarts under sustained burst traffic. We've validated a minimal "heap-guard" micro-patch that limits per-worker heap growth and forces safe eviction of large internal caches.

We need to activate the guard across your dedicated nodes immediately to prevent customer-visible errors. This will be a rolling activation across your nodes and should not interrupt active requests in >99% of cases, but there is a short risk window (~30–90s per host) where in-flight long-response requests may be retried.

What we will do (timeline, immediate):
- 02:30 PST — schedule rolling activation (non-blocking) on your pool (approx 10 hosts).
- Rolling activation strategy: drain-to-safe, apply guard, verify health, rejoin. Typical host step ~45s.
- We'll monitor QoS and immediately roll back if we see regressions.

Action items for you:
- Please confirm any scheduled customer jobs that must not be retried in the next 2 hours.
- If you rely on long-polling inference (>10s per request), flag those endpoints now so we can coordinate an isolated window.

Attachments: activation runbook and a sample heap dump for context.

We're treating this as an incident with high priority; I'll follow up with a short postmortem and timeline once complete.

Thanks —
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: heap-guard-activation-steps.pdf (PDF, 120KB)
Attachment: sample-heap-dump.txt (text, 40KB)
From: Zoe Patel <zoe.patel@acme-analytics.com>

Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 02:22:14 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: Emergency heap-guard activation — short notice maintenance and actions

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for the quick alert. Two questions: 1) Do you expect any API contract changes we need to be aware of? 2) What SLA exposure should we expect for the 30–90s host windows (we have a customer-facing job at 03:00 PST)?

We do have a small set of streaming inference jobs that can run >15s. If rolling activation will touch those hosts, can we pause the job at 02:50 PST?

—Zoe
Zoe Patel
Head of SRE, Acme Analytics
zoe.patel@acme-analytics.com

Subject: Re: Urgent: Emergency heap-guard activation — short notice maintenance and actions

On Tue, Dec 7, 2026 at 2:22 AM Zoe Patel <zoe.patel@acme-analytics.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the quick alert. Two questions: 1) Do you expect any API contract changes we need to be aware of? 2) What SLA exposure should we expect for the 30–90s host windows (we have a customer-facing job at 03:00 PST)?
> 
> We do have a small set of streaming inference jobs that can run >15s. If rolling activation will touch those hosts, can we pause the job at 02:50 PST?

Hi Zoe — quick answers:
- No API contract changes — this is an internal memory-management guard; request/response shapes, headers, and semantics remain identical.
- SLA exposure: we do not expect violation of per-request SLA in normal circumstances, but given your long-tail requests there is a non-zero chance of a request being retried by our framework if its host is in the brief drain window. We estimate <0.05% request impact for your traffic profile; we will mark the activation as non-disruptive and avoid hosts with active streaming sessions where possible.

Please pause the 03:00 customer job if you can; if not, tell us the job ID and we'll exclude its hosts from the first wave and run a second, quieter wave at 03:40 PST.

I'll start the activation at 02:35 PST with a canary host and report status after the canary. Marissa will monitor customer-facing metrics and escalate if needed.

—Priyom

Attachment: heap-guard-activation-steps.pdf (PDF, 120KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Urgent: Emergency heap-guard activation — short notice maintenance and actions

Update: canary completed at 02:40 PST — no service-level anomalies observed (p50/p95/p99 within expected baselines).

I pushed a short smoke-run targeting your main endpoint and validated success rates — 100% success on 120 requests, average latency delta +12ms (within noise). Rolling activation underway; next host 02:46 PST.

Ben and Laura are watching support channels for any customer reports. Zoe — we'll leave your 03:00 job excluded from wave 1 as requested; please confirm when paused and we'll proceed.

—Marissa
